description: I'm Sasi Kiran, a solo participant interested in space, physics and data visualization. For the Flame in Freefall challenge I built PYRO-CORE, a browser app that shows how fire behaves in microgravity. With no gravity there is no rising hot air, so a flame lives only on the air a fan pushes past it, and near its limit it burns dim and blue, easy to miss by eye. PYRO-CORE lets you pick a cabin atmosphere, a material and a fan speed, then see the flame in 3D as your eyes and a thermal camera .
summary:
PYRO-CORE is an interactive web dashboard that turns NASA's microgravity combustion research into clear fire-safety answers for human space exploration. In orbit, hot air does not rise, so a fire lives only on the air that ventilation fans push past it; near its limit it burns dim and blue, easy to miss by eye. Future Moon bases and rovers are expected to use 30% or more oxygen at lower pressure, which makes materials more flammable.

PYRO-CORE ranks and compares 17 NASA combustion investigations (BASS, BASS-II, Saffire, SAME, FLEX, ACME, SoFIE, FM2 and more) for a chosen habitat and fire-safety goal. A 3D simulator, calibrated to NASA's BASS-II result that acrylic burned on the ISS at 13.6% oxygen, shows whether a material can burn in Space Station, Moon Base or Artemis air, as seen by eye and by a thermal camera. It clearly separates what NASA measured from what the model estimates, helping students, researchers and engineers see where flight data exists and where it is still missing.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

PYRO-CORE answers two questions for spacecraft designers, researchers and students: will this material catch fire in this habitat, and what has NASA actually measured about it?

1. NASA investigation explorer: 17 NASA microgravity combustion investigations (BASS, BASS-II, Saffire-I/II/III, SAME and SAME-R, DAFT, FLEX, FLEX-2, CFI, ACME BRE, CFI-G and E-FIELD, SPICE, SLICE, SoFIE, FLARE, LUCI, FM2) are summarized and ranked for a chosen habitat (spacecraft/ISS, Moon Base or rover, Mars, Earth applications) and fire-safety goal (prevention, detection, suppression, predictive modelling). Each ranking shows its reasons, and up to three investigations can be compared side by side by fuel, hardware, test conditions, measurements and whether the data is in NASA PSI yet. Unknown fields are marked "not stated" rather than guessed.

2. Live flame simulator: a 3D flow duct modelled on NASA's BASS-II hardware, with a polymer rod burning at its tip. Users change the cabin atmosphere (ISS 21% O2; Moon Base 30% O2 at 10.2 psi; exploration atmosphere 34% O2 at 8.2 psi; or custom), the material (acrylic, Delrin, Nomex, SIBAL fabric, cotton, silicone) and the fan airflow.

3. Eye vs thermal camera: the same moment rendered as the eye sees it and as a 3.8 µm infrared camera sees it, showing how near-limit flames can be faint to the eye.

4. Where-it-can-burn map, ISS vs Artemis table, guided scenarios (ghost flame, Artemis shift, fan-off quench, blow-off), nitrogen-suppression test, cool-down estimate, evidence briefing, shareable links and CSV export.

HOW IT WORKS

A reduced-order combustion model compares heat released by the flame (Huggett's 13.1 MJ per kg of oxygen) with heat lost by radiation, and uses a Damköhler number in the stretch-rate form NASA researchers used for BASS-II. It is calibrated so acrylic's lowest burning oxygen at ISS pressure equals NASA's measured 13.6%. An automated check fails if the calibration drifts. Rankings use a transparent rule shown on screen. An optional Google Gemini summary may only restate the app's facts; it is rejected automatically if it adds any number not in them.

KEY INSIGHT

In the model, Nomex and silicone cannot burn in ISS air but can burn in both Moon Base and Artemis air. No NASA flight data covers those conditions yet, and the app makes that gap visible.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

It makes decades of NASA results findable, comparable and understandable in one place, supports material selection questions for future habitats, and is honest about limits: every number is labelled as NASA-measured or model estimate, and it is not a safety certification.

CREATIVITY

It combines a ranked research explorer with a live, calibrated physics simulation and a side-by-side eye-versus-thermal view, so users can both read the evidence and see its consequences.

TOOLS

TypeScript, React, Three.js with a custom GLSL ray-marching shader, Recharts, Tailwind CSS, Vite, GitHub Pages, optional Google Gemini API. Open source under the MIT licence.
